what_changed.headline: Energy shock remains the dominant macro swing factor
what_changed.significance: ECB and RBA sources describe a second energy-price wave and persistent inflation pressure; diplomatic headlines point to two-way oil risk, but the reported Iranian proposal is not independently confirmed.
what_changed.transmission: Higher energy prices raise inflation and policy-rate risk; credible de-escalation would reverse part of that impulse.

what_changed.headline: AI optimism is concentrated in selected technology and semiconductor names
what_changed.significance: Meta Muse adoption news was followed by a large rally in Meta and selected CPU and infrastructure stocks, while research cautions that adoption does not yet establish durable monetisation or orders.
what_changed.transmission: Agentic AI could increase cloud CPU and infrastructure demand, but the earnings transmission remains unproven.

what_changed.headline: Treasury-market liquidity infrastructure is being strengthened
what_changed.significance: The Federal Reserve is modernising discount-window access and collateral processes; New York Fed research finds Treasury trading increasingly concentrated around month-end and index-strike times.
what_changed.transmission: Easier collateralised liquidity may reduce forced Treasury sales during stress, while concentration around pricing windows can amplify execution risk.

executive_decisions.development: Keep energy-driven inflation and policy repricing as the primary near-term risk monitor.
executive_decisions.why_it_matters: Central-bank sources describe inflation as higher for longer or elevated, while oil headlines remain highly reversible.
executive_decisions.transmission: Energy prices affect inflation expectations, central-bank reaction functions, real incomes and risk appetite.

executive_decisions.development: Treat the AI rally as selective rather than broad confirmation of a durable earnings cycle.
executive_decisions.why_it_matters: The evidence is mainly early product adoption and market interpretation; causal revenue and capacity evidence is incomplete.
executive_decisions.transmission: Potential infrastructure demand supports selected hardware and cloud exposures, but concentration increases reversal risk.

themes.title: Energy shock versus disinflation
themes.implication: Maintain a two-sided framework: upside energy risk threatens rates and risk assets; a verified supply or diplomatic improvement would support duration and cyclical risk.

themes.title: Agentic AI and concentration
themes.implication: Selected CPU and infrastructure exposures may benefit, while concentration and valuation-reversal risks remain material.

themes.title: Energy-driven inflation versus growth
themes.implication: Rates retain upside inflation sensitivity while growth-sensitive assets face demand risk; oil can soften tactically without resolving physical tightness.

themes.title: Fiscal credibility and sovereign term premia
themes.implication: French duration and spread exposure remain vulnerable to political or budget setbacks.

themes.title: Energy shock meets policy normalization
themes.implication: Front-end rates remain vulnerable to upside inflation surprises, but weaker real incomes create a later growth downside.

themes.title: AI investment: productivity promise versus concentration risk
themes.implication: AI-linked equities retain a supportive fundamental narrative, while duration and credit are exposed to investment-financing and valuation shocks.

themes.title: Renewed US tightening versus persistent inflation risk
themes.implication: Supports USD and short-end yields; creates a higher hurdle for duration and long-duration equities.

themes.title: Energy shock as the cross-asset policy variable
themes.implication: Persistent energy strength would prolong tightening risk; normalization would reopen disinflation and easing scenarios.

themes.title: AI investment, growth and fiscal crowding-out
themes.implication: Supports selective exposure to durable productivity beneficiaries while cautioning against treating AI as a complete macro or fiscal solution.

themes.title: Energy shock, fiscal supply and the duration premium
themes.implication: The combination is adverse for long-duration rates and rate-sensitive equities, while supporting near-term USD demand; confirmation requires continued energy and yield data.

themes.title: Japan normalization and global duration spillovers
themes.implication: The yen and JGB curve remain sensitive to the balance between faster normalization and fiscal/financial-stability concerns.

themes.title: Energy shock versus policy credibility
themes.implication: Upside risk to front-end and inflation-sensitive rates; downside risk to energy-importing growth assets; dollar support is possible but not assured.

themes.title: AI investment, productivity and financing strain
themes.implication: Supports selective AI infrastructure exposure over the medium term but raises duration, credit and equity-correction risks.

themes.title: Energy supply shock becomes a policy shock
themes.implication: Near-term bias remains toward higher inflation risk, tighter policy expectations and pressure on duration; growth-sensitive assets remain vulnerable if the shock persists.

themes.title: AI investment supports activity but raises capital-intensity and valuation questions
themes.implication: Infrastructure beneficiaries may remain supported, while software and credit exposures require proof of monetisation.

themes.title: Energy shock meets restrictive policy
themes.implication: Policy rates can remain high even as growth weakens, increasing duration and cyclical-equity sensitivity.

themes.title: Long-end yield pressure is becoming a cross-asset constraint
themes.implication: Duration, credit and rate-sensitive equities remain vulnerable if yields continue higher.

themes.title: AI investment cycle: strong demand, uncertain monetisation
themes.implication: The cycle supports semiconductors and selected infrastructure, while financing needs and model-price competition create credit and equity dispersion.
